title: Annotatio VI §.VIII: Reformed need not ‘return’ — they always confessed substantial presence
pass_a_gloss: Wherefore this one thing remains — not that the Reformed, error acknowledged, change a sentence they never held, and return to a way from which they never deflected, and confess with open and ingenuous words the true and substantial presence of Christ’s body and blood in the Holy Supper — not with words insidiously conceived and composed to deceive men — which presence they have never not confessed, without all tergiversation or hesitation, and will confess to all eternity.
pass_b_english: What remains is not that the Reformed ‘admit error’ and return to a path they never left.
They have always, without tergiversation, confessed true substantial presence in open words — and will forever.
source_text: Quapropter hoc unum restat, non, ut Reformati, agnito errore, mutent sententiam, quam nunquam habuerunt, redeántque in viam, à qua nunquam deflexerunt, & veram substantialémque corporis & sanguinis Christi in S. Cœna præsentiam, non verbis insidiose conceptis & ad homines decipiendos compositis, sed apertis & ingenuis fateantur, quam nunquam non, citra omnem tergiversationem aut hæsitantiam, fassi sunt, & in omnem æternitatem fatebuntur.
